_meta.description: Tripwires. Each falsifier names the limb it kills, the observable condition that would trip it, the positions it retires, and its current state. A thesis without these is a narrative.
_meta.state_scale: armed = watching, no evidence yet / warming = partial evidence accumulating / tripped = condition met, positions must be retired
_meta.discipline_note: The point of writing the exit in advance is that it is written before the money is at risk. A falsifier that gets renegotiated when it trips was never a falsifier.
_meta.reading_note: Evidence read against primary sources on 2026-08-07. None of the falsifiers tripped; two moved further from tripping and one is unchanged at 'warming'. A falsifier moving away from its condition is worth recording explicitly — it is the only thing that distinguishes a thesis being tested from a thesis being asserted.

falsifiers.n: Immigration surge relieves the constrained occupations
falsifiers.condition: Sustained net immigration growth, concentrated in healthcare support, construction trades and personal care, held for more than four consecutive quarters — combined with visible deceleration in services wage growth relative to goods.
falsifiers.kills: Limb C outright, and with it the portfolio-construction conclusion. Also repairs limb D's and limb H's cost problem, which paradoxically helps the care operators while destroying the labour thesis.
falsifiers.note: The single largest swing factor in the thesis. It is also the reason limb C and the substitution sleeve must be sized as one correlated bet rather than two positions.
falsifiers.evidence: EVIDENCE 2026-08-07: moving away from tripping. The 2026 Trustees Report lowered its assumed immigration levels — one of three revisions that widened the 75-year deficit by 16%. That is an assumption change by federal actuaries rather than an outturn, so it is suggestive rather than decisive, and actual flow data still needs reading. But the direction is against this falsifier. Still the largest single swing factor in the thesis and still the reason limb C and the substitution sleeve must be sized as one correlated bet.

falsifiers.condition: Labour force participation among 65+ continuing to rise rather than flattening, sustained across a full business cycle rather than a single tight-labour episode.
falsifiers.kills: Limb C's premise and limb D's timing simultaneously — the labour does not leave, and the consumption rotation is deferred with it.
retires: The labour sleeve entirely, plus the timing on the limb D relay — the go-go fade would need to be pushed right by however long participation keeps rising.
falsifiers.note: The highest-value single indicator on the dashboard, because it tests two limbs at once. Read it together with f1: if both move against the thesis simultaneously, the labour argument is finished.
falsifiers.evidence: EVIDENCE 2026-08-07: moving away from tripping. 65+ participation is 18.7% (June 2026) against a 2019 annual peak of 20.2% and a 2024 average of 19.5%. Participation peaked before the pandemic and has not recovered — people are not, in aggregate, working longer. This is the single highest-value reading on the dashboard and it currently supports limb C.

falsifiers.n: Morbidity compression — the care curve moves right
falsifiers.condition: Health utilisation per capita in the 75+ bands flattening or falling on a sustained basis, with GLP-1 and successor therapies visibly reducing the chronic disease burden that drives care intensity.
falsifiers.kills: Limb D's volume assumption. Lengthens the go-go band — which would rescue the experience-economy names this thesis is fading — and shortens the high-cost tail that limb H and the care operators depend on.
retires: portions of the WELL/VTR occupancy case
RGA's longevity book takes a loss
falsifiers.note: Marked warming rather than armed because the evidence is genuinely accumulating — GLP-1 effects on the elderly disease burden are real, if slower and more nuanced than the initial market reaction assumed. LLY is held partly as the internal hedge against this. Watch ResMed's multiple as the market's live pricing of it.
falsifiers.evidence: EVIDENCE 2026-08-07 (CMS Geographic Variation PUF, 2014-2024): tested directly and NOT confirmed as stated. Per-capita institutional utilisation among FFS 65+ did fall hard — SNF days/1k -31%, home health visits -32%, inpatient days -18% — which looks superficially like compression. But ambulatory contact rose over the same window: E&M visits/1k +16%, imaging +12%, procedures +5%. A healthier elderly population would see doctors LESS, not more. The pattern is site-of-care shift plus payment policy (SNF PDPM 2019, home health PDGM 2020), not people getting well. f3 as written therefore remains unproven — but the testing surfaced a different and larger risk, carried as f11.

falsifiers.n: The crude decumulation story turns out to be right
falsifiers.condition: Sustained net equity outflow attributable to the 65+ cohort showing up in flow-of-funds data, without an offsetting inflow elsewhere — a genuine supply shock rather than a composition change.
falsifiers.kills: Limb A's benign reading, and inverts it. The composition trade becomes a directional bear case on equity multiples.
retires: and would argue for reducing gross equity exposure across every other limb
falsifiers.note: Low probability on the evidence to date — wealth concentration and reinvestment of RMDs have historically overwhelmed this — but very high impact, because it would change the thesis from a rotation into a de-risking.

falsifiers.condition: Retention data showing wirehouses and incumbent advisors keeping heir relationships at high rates, alongside slowing independent-channel recruitment and share gain.
falsifiers.kills: Limb B's share-shift argument. What remains is a levered bet on AUM beta wearing a demographic costume.
retires: and reduces MS and RJF to ordinary quality-franchise holdings
falsifiers.note: Cerulli channel data is the honest adjudicator here; company recruiting disclosures are the fast but self-serving read.

falsifiers.condition: A structural reduction in Medicare or Medicaid rates for post-acute, home health or skilled nursing — or a Medicare Advantage benchmark reset that persistently runs below medical cost trend.
falsifiers.kills: The reimbursed half of limb D. Does not touch volume, which is the point of the whole private-pay tilt.
retires: The direct-rate-exposure tier in the reimbursement map, sized down or out — payors first, then the Medicaid-dependent operators
falsifiers.note: This is the falsifier the portfolio is already built around rather than one that would surprise it. The private-pay tilt exists precisely so that this event is survivable rather than fatal.

falsifiers.condition: Existing-home turnover in retirement metros staying suppressed even as the cohort ages through the transition bands, with homeowner tenure among 65+ continuing to lengthen.
falsifiers.kills: The inventory-release half of limb H, and defers senior housing move-in rates.
retires: Reduces the BKD occupancy case and the silver-inventory framing; leaves the aging-in-place trade intact and arguably strengthens it
falsifiers.note: Deliberately cuts both ways — the same reading that damages the inventory thesis supports the home-modification and in-home-care positions. Not a portfolio-level event.

falsifiers.condition: Nursing programme places, apprenticeship completions and residency slots expanding faster than the 85+ population — the capacity gap closing rather than widening.
falsifiers.kills: The strongest 'why isn't this priced' mechanism in the thesis. Without it, limbs C and H lose their pricing-power argument and become ordinary cyclicals.
retires: and removes the durable-moat premium from the contractor names
falsifiers.note: Slow-moving and highly measurable — applications turned away is the single number that matters. This is the most checkable falsifier on the list and deserves an annual diary entry.
falsifiers.evidence: EVIDENCE 2026-08-07: not tripping. AACN counted 93,000 qualified nursing applications turned away in 2025, including nearly 17,000 from graduate programmes — and since most full-time faculty roles require a graduate degree, the constraint reproduces itself. Capacity is not responding faster than demand. This is the most checkable falsifier on the list and it currently supports the capacity-gap mechanism.

falsifiers.condition: Legislation that materially extends trust-fund solvency — benefit formula change, means-testing, retirement age adjustment or a payroll tax cap change — passing with durable political support.
falsifiers.kills: Limb E's step-function risk, in a way that is mostly good for the rest of the book.
retires: Nothing directly. It would compress the reimbursement risk premium embedded in the limb D book, which argues for increasing rather than reducing exposure to the direct-rate tier.
falsifiers.note: The one falsifier whose triggering would improve most of the portfolio. Included because a thesis should name the scenarios where it is wrong in a profitable direction too.

falsifiers.condition: The 'why isn't this priced' test in the thesis failing limb by limb — capacity responding, no policy discontinuity materialising, institutional lag closing, and relative valuations already reflecting the forward earnings gradient.
falsifiers.kills: The premise of the entire dashboard. Demographics being forecastable is the reason to be sceptical of demographic theses, including this one.
retires: Everything. This is the exit, not a rotation.
falsifiers.note: The honest master falsifier. If the four mechanisms in the not-priced test all fail, the correct conclusion is that a forty-year-old known fact is in the price and the edge was imagined. Review this one deliberately rather than letting it be absorbed by the individual limb reviews.

falsifiers.n: The per-capita offset consumes the population arithmetic
falsifiers.condition: Per-capita institutional utilisation continuing to decline at anything close to its 2014-2024 rate — SNF days/1k -3.6% a year, home health visits -3.8% a year — such that aggregate volume growth stays in the low single digits despite the 85+ population compounding at ~4.6% a year.
falsifiers.kills: Not limb D's direction, but the naive version of its magnitude. The demographic tailwind is real and the age gradient is steeper than assumed (SNF days/1k: 7.0x at 85+ versus 65-74). What it kills is the assumption that population growth passes through to volumes. Institutional operators are where that error is most expensive.
retires: Reprices rather than retires. Reduces institutional and facility-based exposure — ENSG, NHC, EHC, and the SNF net-lease REITs OHI, CTRE, SBRA — in favour of ambulatory, hospice and private-pay, where per-capita utilisation is flat to rising.
falsifiers.note: Discovered on 2026-08-07 while testing f3, and larger than the falsifier that prompted the test. This is the first genuinely unanticipated risk the sourcing programme has produced — the v1 thesis multiplied population growth straight through to care volumes and never asked whether utilisation per head was constant. It was not.
falsifiers.evidence: EVIDENCE 2026-08-07: partially realised, not hypothetical. Compounding the observed -3.6% a year per-capita SNF decline against +4.6% a year 85+ population growth gives roughly +12% aggregate SNF days over 2025-2040, versus the +96% population alone implies. Hospice is the exception at +21% per capita over the decade. Caveat in both directions: the decline is partly payment-policy driven and cannot continue indefinitely (there is a floor), while MA selection and rising average age both bias the measured decline toward understatement. REVISED 2026-08-07 against SEC filings: this is a market-SIZE warning, not a company-revenue prediction, and the distinction matters more than the finding. Care-delivery revenue compounded at a 9.9% median over CY2019-CY2025 — ENSG 16.4%, PNTG 18.7%, OPCH 16.1% — straight through the decade when per-capita SNF days fell 31%. The sector is fragmented enough that disciplined consolidators outgrow a shrinking per-capita market for years. Severity cut from 3 to 2, and the ENSG downgrade it triggered has been reversed.

falsifiers.n: Skilled-trades scarcity does not show up in wages
falsifiers.condition: Construction and extraction wages continuing to run at or below the all-civilian baseline. If licensed trade labour were genuinely scarce and irreplaceable, it should command a rising relative wage. It is not doing so.
falsifiers.kills: The contractor and trades-training sleeve — the half of limb C that is not about care labour. Does not touch the care side, which the same data confirms emphatically.
retires: and reduces the trades half of LINC and UTI. FIX, APG and LMB are less exposed because their mix leans toward installation, maintenance and repair, which IS running above baseline at +3.0pp.
falsifiers.note: Found 2026-08-07 testing limb C's inflation claim. The claim was written as one limb; the data says it is two, and only one of them is supported. The contractor names were already froth-3 with no margin of safety on price — now the mechanism underneath them is unevidenced too.
falsifiers.evidence: EVIDENCE 2026-08-07 (BLS ECI, 2019Q4-2026Q2): construction & extraction occupations +27.6% cumulative versus an all-civilian baseline of +28.3%, and the construction industry +26.7%, the slowest of ten cuts examined. Manufacturing beat both. Confound: construction demand was weak over part of the window, so this may be a demand signal rather than evidence against scarcity — that is a reason to keep the falsifier at warming rather than tripped, not a reason to dismiss it. REVISED 2026-08-07 against SEC filings: the wage channel is still unevidenced, but the margin channel is strongly evidenced and points the other way. Contractor operating margins expanded a median 5.1pp over CY2019-CY2025 — APG +23.3pp, IESC +7.5pp, LMB +6.1pp, EME +5.1pp, FIX +4.4pp — on revenue growth of 10-42%. That is pricing power. Either the binding constraint is contractor CAPACITY rather than labour cost, or it is the construction cycle. Both readings undercut 'reduce because the mechanism is absent'. Severity cut from 3 to 2 and the reduction softened.
